key_insight: A three-agent AI framework links high-level network intents to adaptive optimization and fast runtime control.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help autonomous mobile networks adapt control policies to changing service requirements and network conditions.
method: A language-model interpreter translates and refines intents into machine-readable optimization templates.
A Bayesian optimizer adapts controller policies to intent specifications.
A multi-objective reinforcement-learning controller makes fast network decisions.
evidence_signal: A radio resource management case study for differentiated connectivity demonstrates adaptability, but the abstract reports no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Deployment would require validating intent translations and ensuring policy adaptation preserves network safety and service constraints.
paper_title: Agentic AI for Intent Management and Control in Autonomous Communication Networks
